drafted_from: tool:roll-back-a-servers-receptionist's row in tools/renew-a-tls-certificate/tool-rows.json, do-work/renew-a-tls-certificate.mjs, do-work/tls-host-owner.py and the tests in test/
start_here: Say to your AI: "Roll back the receptionist release cccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccc on my server at 192.0.2.34, it starts but is wrong." It runs tool:roll-back-a-servers-receptionist and checks the service through public TLS.
no_lists_because: It keeps no list of its own: it takes one server's facts as its input and answers what that server's certificate owner reports.
instructions: 1. Gather the server's facts: its public name, IPv4 address, SSH port, the administrator you sign in as, its pinned key ("<address> ssh-ed25519 <key>") and its layout (host: owner path, state folder, downloads folder, ingress, receptionist). The README in tools/renew-a-tls-certificate/ shows a made-up one.

2. Say to your AI the sentence in start_here. It calls run_resource_operation at @workshop-tools with method tools:run, tool tool:roll-back-a-servers-receptionist and that input (the worked example shows one). The door mounts your server administration key for the run; you paste no key.

3. Read what comes back: {"rolled_back": "<the commit>", "current": "<the release now current, or null when the seed starts>"}. An {"error": ...} or a thrown message names what to change (for example the layout or the pinned key was refused).
4. commit is required and must be 40 hex characters; anything else is refused. The refused release is never taken again by any host.

worked_examples.title: Refuse a wrong release
worked_examples.given: From tools/renew-a-tls-certificate/test/tls-host-owner.test.py (a rollback runs the program's own verb as its account): the program answers current ffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffff for refused commit cccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccc, then the service restarts and is checked.
